newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia sacks head of Supreme Court -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Croatia sacks head of Supreme Court -- paper.

text.p: Croatia's State Judicial Council has sacked the president of the Supreme Court for bringing the court and the office of judge into disrepute, a local newspaper reported on Wednesday.

Zagreb daily Vjesnik said the Council took the decision to fire Krunislav Olujic on Tuesday after a disciplinary hearing. The Supreme Court chief had been suspended last November following accusations of paedophilia.

Vjesnik said the Council cleared Olujic of suspicion of paedophilia but found him guilty of tarnishing the reputation of the court and the office of judge by appearing in public with two known criminals. He has 15 days to appeal.
The Council decision climaxed a protracted legal process that has caused uproar in Croatian political life.
Olujic was one of the closest aides of President Franjo Tudjman. At different times he has been a parliament deputy, state prosecutor and head of Croatian intelligence services.
It was the first time a high-ranking official in Croatia has been publicly accused of sexual offences, with proceedings against him based on taps of his private phone calls.
Although disciplinary hearings were conducted behind closed doors, contents of the recordings were published in the Tuesday edition of the Zagreb weekly Globus.
Olujic and his lawyers have argued that the affair was politically motivated and that recordings of his private telephone conversations were inadmissible as evidence as they were obtained illegally.
Political commentators have speculated that Olujic had to be removed from the sensitive position of Supreme Court president ahead of local and presidential elections due in 1997.
